\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تقلب} (taqallaba)}{تقلب (taqallaba)}]{\ar{تقلب} (taqallaba) — to keep changing; to fluctuate}

\label{lesson:AR-C486-taqallaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to shine, then the Arabic for to grow dark.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تقلب}}
\textbf{\ar{تقلب}} — \emph{taqallaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to keep changing; to fluctuate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يتقلب} \ar{الطقس} \ar{كثيرا} \ar{في} \ar{الربيع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yataqallabu aṭ-ṭaqs kathīran fī ar-rabīʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather changes a lot in spring.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتقلب}, \emph{yataqallab}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تقلب}} (\emph{taqallaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-l-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to turn over\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, \textquotedblleft{}to turn this way and that\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taqallaba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taqallaba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yataqallabu aṭ-ṭaqs kathīran fī ar-rabīʿ.} — The weather changes a lot in spring.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to shine, then the Arabic for to grow dark, then say \emph{taqallaba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تقلب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To keep changing; to fluctuate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تدهور} (tadahwara)}{تدهور (tadahwara)}]{\ar{تدهور} (tadahwara) — to get worse; to deteriorate}

\label{lesson:AR-C486-tadahwara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to grow dark, then the Arabic for to keep changing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تدهور}}
\textbf{\ar{تدهور}} — \emph{tadahwara} — \textquotedblleft{}to get worse; to deteriorate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تدهور} \ar{الطقس} \ar{فعدنا} \ar{إلى} \ar{الفندق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tadahwara aṭ-ṭaqs fa-ʿudnā ilā al-funduq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather got worse, so we went back to the hotel.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتدهور}, \emph{yatadahwar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تدهور}} (\emph{tadahwara}) is a verb with four root letters; the origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تساقط} (tasāqaṭa)}{تساقط (tasāqaṭa)}]{\ar{تساقط} (tasāqaṭa) — to fall steadily (of snow or leaves)}

\label{lesson:AR-C486-tasaqata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to keep changing, then the Arabic for to get worse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تساقط}}
\textbf{\ar{تساقط}} — \emph{tasāqaṭa} — \textquotedblleft{}to fall steadily (of snow or leaves)\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tasāqaṭa ath-thalj fī al-layl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتساقط}, \emph{yatasāqaṭ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تساقط}} (\emph{tasāqaṭa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-q-ṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}to fall\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VI, \textquotedblleft{}to fall one after another\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{منعش} (munʿish)}{منعش (munʿish)}]{\ar{منعش} (munʿish) — refreshing}

\label{lesson:AR-C486-munish}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to get worse, then the Arabic for to fall steadily.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{منعش}}
\textbf{\ar{منعش}} — \emph{munʿish} — \textquotedblleft{}refreshing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{الهواء} \ar{في} \ar{الصباح} \ar{منعشا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna al-hawāʾ fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ munʿishan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The morning air was refreshing.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{منعش}} (\emph{munʿish}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-ʿ-sh}, \textquotedblleft{}to raise up, to revive\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the Form IV participle, \textquotedblleft{}that revives\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تعرض} (taʿarraḍa)}{تعرض (taʿarraḍa)}]{\ar{تعرض} (taʿarraḍa) — to be exposed (to); to suffer}

\label{lesson:AR-C486-taarrada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to fall steadily, then the Arabic for refreshing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تعرض}}
\textbf{\ar{تعرض}} — \emph{taʿarraḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}to be exposed (to); to suffer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تعرض} \ar{المسافرون} \ar{للمطر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʿarraḍa al-musāfirūn li-l-maṭar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The travellers were caught in the rain.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتعرض}, \emph{yataʿarraḍ}.

It takes \emph{li-}: \emph{taʿarraḍa li-}, \textquotedblleft{}to be exposed to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تعرض}} (\emph{taʿarraḍa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-r-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}to show, to present\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, \textquotedblleft{}to put oneself in the way of\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 479–486 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R486-review-479-486}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for to ski and a wild beast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to ski, a wild beast, a plastic bag, to exchange, to pack
  \item a weather forecast, a degree, to increase, to drop, mild
  \item a shower of rain, drizzle, a downpour, to pour down, to clear up
  \item a breeze, a hurricane, to blow hard, to grow stronger, danger
  \item coldness, chilly, biting, frost, to get cold
  \item a heatwave, stifling, humidity, drought, to evaporate
  \item clear weather, a rainbow, dew, to shine, to grow dark
  \item to keep changing, to get worse, to fall steadily, refreshing, to be exposed
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To ski? (\textbf{\ar{تزلج}}, \emph{tazallaja}.) A wild beast? (\textbf{\ar{وحش}}, \emph{waḥsh}.) A plastic bag? (\textbf{\ar{كيس}}, \emph{kīs}.) To exchange? (\textbf{\ar{تبادل}}, \emph{tabādala}.) To pack? (\textbf{\ar{حزم}}, \emph{ḥazama}.) A weather forecast? (\textbf{\ar{نشرة} \ar{جوية}}, \emph{nashra jawwiyya}.) A degree? (\textbf{\ar{درجة}}, \emph{daraja}.) To increase? (\textbf{\ar{ارتفع}}, \emph{irtafaʿa}.) To drop? (\textbf{\ar{انخفض}}, \emph{inkhafaḍa}.) Mild? (\textbf{\ar{معتدل}}, \emph{muʿtadil}.) A shower of rain? (\textbf{\ar{زخة}}, \emph{zakhkha}.) Drizzle? (\textbf{\ar{رذاذ}}, \emph{radhādh}.) A downpour? (\textbf{\ar{وابل}}, \emph{wābil}.) To pour down? (\textbf{\ar{هطل}}, \emph{haṭala}.) To clear up? (\textbf{\ar{صفا}}, \emph{ṣafā}.) A breeze? (\textbf{\ar{نسيم}}, \emph{nasīm}.) A hurricane? (\textbf{\ar{إعصار}}, \emph{iʿṣār}.) To blow hard? (\textbf{\ar{عصف}}, \emph{ʿaṣafa}.) To grow stronger? (\textbf{\ar{اشتد}}, \emph{ishtadda}.) Danger? (\textbf{\ar{خطر}}, \emph{khaṭar}.) Coldness? (\textbf{\ar{برودة}}, \emph{burūda}.) Chilly? (\textbf{\ar{بارد}}, \emph{bārid}.) Biting? (\textbf{\ar{قارس}}, \emph{qāris}.) Frost? (\textbf{\ar{صقيع}}, \emph{ṣaqīʿ}.) To get cold? (\textbf{\ar{برد}}, \emph{barada}.) A heatwave? (\textbf{\ar{موجة} \ar{حر}}, \emph{mawjat ḥarr}.) Stifling? (\textbf{\ar{خانق}}, \emph{khāniq}.) Humidity? (\textbf{\ar{رطوبة}}, \emph{ruṭūba}.) Drought? (\textbf{\ar{جفاف}}, \emph{jafāf}.) To evaporate? (\textbf{\ar{تبخر}}, \emph{tabakhkhara}.) Clear weather? (\textbf{\ar{صحو}}, \emph{ṣaḥw}.) A rainbow? (\textbf{\ar{قوس} \ar{قزح}}, \emph{qaws quzaḥ}.) Dew? (\textbf{\ar{ندى}}, \emph{nadā}.) To shine? (\textbf{\ar{أشرق}}, \emph{ashraqa}.) To grow dark? (\textbf{\ar{أظلم}}, \emph{aẓlama}.) To keep changing? (\textbf{\ar{تقلب}}, \emph{taqallaba}.) To get worse? (\textbf{\ar{تدهور}}, \emph{tadahwara}.) To fall steadily? (\textbf{\ar{تساقط}}, \emph{tasāqaṭa}.) Refreshing? (\textbf{\ar{منعش}}, \emph{munʿish}.) To be exposed? (\textbf{\ar{تعرض}}, \emph{taʿarraḍa}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
